hypothesis_update: The primary defect hypothesis is in the multi-component name-resolution path used by rewrite_compose_statements: when a compose-level init statement references a bare name that is a state variable or const in more than one loaded component, the function either (a) silently resolves to the first component in BTreeMap (alphabetical alias) order producing a wrong prefix, (b) fails to resolve and emits an unprefixed name that will not match any kernel variable, or (c) lacks the collision check entirely. A secondary hypothesis is that composed_kernel may emit duplicate items or incorrect ordering when static_items already contains a SpecItem::Init from a component and the function also appends the collected init at line 360-364.
rationale: The target body shows two distinct rewrite paths for init statements: component-level init at line 315 calls rewrite_statements(statements, component, &HashSet::new()) in the context of a single component, while compose-level init at line 345 calls rewrite_compose_statements(statements, &components) in the context of all components. The multi-component resolution path is the most likely site for a data-integrity defect: if a state or const name exists in two different components, the resolution semantics (error, first-match, ambiguity) are unresolved. Additionally, this card contains composed_kernel (line 366 call site), the final assembly function where ordering, deduplication, or item-loss bugs would produce an incorrect KernelSpec. The card also covers rewrite_compose_item (line 352), which handles all other ComposeItem::Common variants and is the only path for those items — a bug there would silently corrupt non-init common items. No other un-received card combines all three of these risk surfaces.
